amendments.because: The Windows outcome is seen only in the on-demand or nightly full run, after merge; pull requests and main pushes run Linux
amendments.done_when: The merge stub commits its message from stdin and the boundary stub reads stdin as UTF-8, so the pull-request body tests pass on Windows as on Linux

done_when: The merge stub commits its message from stdin and the boundary stub reads stdin as UTF-8, the way Forge sends a pull request body

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The proof list says the Windows outcome is proven by main's full run after merge, but `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml` runs the full suite on Linux only for pushes to main. Pull-request tests in `.github/workflows/forge.yml` also use Ubuntu; the Windows pull-request job runs only an installer test. Neither named pull-request body test has the claimed Windows check behind it, so the Windows proof is hollow.
findings.title: Not done: proof list

why: The pull-request body tests fail on Windows: one stub commits a 65 KB message on the command line, past Windows' limit, and another reads stdin with the Windows code page
